Curriculum coverage

Primary maths practice, organised by year and topic.

KickMaths is built for UK primary pupils. Its Year 1–6 content map uses England’s National Curriculum for mathematics, so families and teachers can select specific extra practice rather than guess what a maths game covers.

What does KickMaths cover?

Key Stage 1: Years 1–2

Counting, place value, addition, subtraction, early multiplication and division, fractions, measures, shapes and simple data.

Lower Key Stage 2: Years 3–4

Times tables, written calculations, fractions and decimals, measures, geometry, coordinates and statistics.

Upper Key Stage 2: Years 5–6

Larger and decimal calculations, fractions and percentages, ratio, introductory algebra, geometry, measures and statistics.

Year 1

Counting and place value to 100

Addition, subtraction and number bonds to 20. Equal groups, halves, quarters, time, money, measures and shapes.

View Year 1 mathsYear 2

Two-digit place value and calculation

The 2, 5 and 10 times tables and related division. Fractions, money, five-minute time, measures and simple charts.

View Year 2 mathsYear 3

The 3, 4 and 8 times tables and related division

Three-digit numbers, column addition and subtraction. Tenths, fractions, time, perimeter and data.

View Year 3 mathsYear 4

All times tables up to 12 × 12

Four-digit column methods, fractions and decimals. Area, angles, symmetry, coordinates and graphs.

View Year 4 mathsYear 5

Long multiplication and short division

Large numbers, fractions, decimals and percentages. Measurement, angles, transformations and line graphs.

View Year 5 mathsYear 6

Long division and multi-step calculations

Fractions, percentages, ratio and introductory algebra. Four-quadrant coordinates, area, volume, pie charts and mean.

View Year 6 maths

Check the actual skills for each year.

Each year page lists the practice families available in the game. Coach checks supporting skills when an answer suggests a gap. Pupils can also choose a specific topic to practise, while parents and teachers can inspect the learning evidence in the Parent report.

Using KickMaths across the UK.

England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland organise their curricula differently. The published year map here is for England. For a pupil following another UK curriculum, choose the skills and level that fit their school’s teaching. The mathematics topics can still provide useful extra practice.

Digital practice and practical learning.

A screen cannot check every part of primary mathematics. Talking through methods, handling objects, measuring and making shapes remain important. The game’s grown-up area includes practical checks, and its skill reports describe evidence from practice rather than an official school attainment judgement.
